actualConversation.question: How can I turn my tutor’s comments on the campus study-space report into a practical revision plan before the prototype review?
actualConversation.answer:
Start by using the tutor’s comments to clarify the link between each requirement and the evidence. The report notes that the power-access requirement needs a clear example tied to interview data. Add that example to show how the feature responds to student needs.

Next, separate participant statements from inferences. The feedback highlights the need to distinguish preferences from design rules. Use the clarity of the decision-making themes to guide the structure.

Finally, incorporate the recommendation to display availability. The tutor points out that outdated data could confuse students. Map this idea to the report’s limitations and include a note on how stale information might affect planning.

Plan your revision by reviewing each requirement against the coded observations. Use the traceability table mentioned in the reflection to document connections between findings and recommendations.
